terminal.scope: Four observed historical eager carriers with eight request-specific TTFTs; include all preceding carriers through each request first token. Fixed surrounding work and request admission; all affected work and replacement time inside the specified region may be eliminated.
terminal.payload_scope: Each TP member’s replicated logical output, including self. New upper assumes compact local normalized selected unique rows, padded to the largest owner count; deduplicate and map back to original head order. Selectors, row maps, launch overhead and wire traffic excluded. Conditional on the full raw snapshot having no other live reader and no prompt-score demands beyond those selected. No projected service speedup.
terminal.method: whole_16_rank_span uses the conservative latest corrected end minus earliest corrected start across participants, maximizing over bounded clock offsets per carrier. within_TP_then_latest_DP assumes independent TP tails and at most one latest-DP join per carrier. rank_local_only holds arrivals and other work fixed. These envelopes include unchanged work, waits and possible idle gaps.
limits: Clock offset bounds depend on the saved F21 causality and constant-offset model; the globally widest envelope is deliberately optimistic. No service speed improvement is inferred.

For M416 DP1 all eight ranks have no frozen vocabulary projection before the following draft decoder starts. Eight later matching projections are outside the priced immediate target readout. Other potential state consumers are still open. Changes to later readers, future steps, buffer ownership or adjacent request scheduling need their own scope.

draft.scope: Same four joint168 carriers and eight original requests; shared target/draft widths are disambiguated by exact task IDs and the intervening three-layer decoder. The eight DP1 projections occur inside the verified draft suffix. Prior-only vs inclusive brackets test when draft steps can affect first-token release; they do not establish the CPU send/receive edge, absence of other observers, or equal service behavior.
limits: Each scope erases all timed work and gaps inside its declared boundaries. Nested scopes overlap. A TP latest join is conditional on the distributed scheduling and resource assumptions; keep the separate clock-bounded 16-rank envelope.
The 32 extra decoder triples are placed relative to the four carriers using matching rank clocks. Their callers and request identities are not inferred.

draft_resource_accounting.scope: Same historical rank clock within each native bracket. Merge complete duration of all typed compute tasks and HCCL envelopes on all streams, including overlap and any protocol waiting. Charge the largest one-rank removable duration per carrier, then recompute the eight request maximum. This sensitivity fixes other arrivals, resource placement, and launch gaps; distributed causal chains with migrating critical ranks require a larger bound.
limits: The complement may include launch gaps, untyped DMA, runtime tasks or synchronization. Its presence does not prove host stalls or that it is removable.
The unpaired triples are separately measured and stay outside the matched request price. A fused expert duration includes its internal communication. Categories may overlap.

draft_expert_arrivals.scope: Fixed first published inputs and original kernel-entry times; all ranks still participate in each draft EP16 call. Even if everything from the last member entry to the last exit is made free, sum the upper bound per sequential layer and recompute clients. The bound for latest exit minus latest entry is max_i min_j(end_i-start_j+u[i,j]); capped by maximum same-rank elapsed. Clock assumptions from the matched carrier cohort only.
limits: An implementation that starts transport, expert work or another rank earlier, alters when other operations can retire, or fuses upstream producers has a different boundary. The count-exchange conservative clock model is not chip hardware clock calibration.
